record.original_question: Define discrepancy of an n x n matrix A by disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity. For square matrices whose columns have unit l2 norm, does there exist a universal constant K such that disc(A) <= K for every such matrix A?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10 (K´omlos Conjecture). There exists a universal constant K such that, for all square matrices A whose columns have unit ℓ2 norm, disc(A) ≤ K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real $n\times n$ matrix $A$, define its discrepancy by
$$\operatorname{disc}(A) \;=\; \inf_{x\in\{-1,+1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty.$$
Does there exist a universal constant $K>0$ (independent of $n$) such that, for every positive integer $n$ and every real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ whose columns each have Euclidean ($\ell_2$) norm equal to $1$, one has
$$\operatorname{disc}(A) \le K\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Komlós conjecture is widely regarded as open as of 2024–2026. The best known upper bound remains Banaszczyk's O(√log n), with an algorithmic version due to Bansal–Dadush–Garg. The best known lower bound on the constant K is approximately 1+√2 (Kunisky, 2021). No proof of a uniform O(1) bound has appeared.

status_evidence.title: The Discrepancy of Unsatisfiable Matrices and a Lower Bound for the Komlós Conjecture Constant
status_evidence.snippet: explicit matrices with columns having unit ℓ² norm and discrepancy approaching 1+√2, the strongest known lower bound on the constant in the Komlós conjecture
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured constant K must be at least 1+√2; conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: An Algorithm for Komlós Conjecture Matching Banaszczyk's Bound
status_evidence.snippet: algorithmic O(log^{1/2} n) bound for the Komlós setting
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound is O(√log n); the O(1) conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024
status_evidence.snippet: The Komlós conjecture remains listed as an open question of interest
